definitions.explanation: A green bell pepper. In Japanese, ピーマン typically refers to the smaller, thinner-walled green peppers common in Asian cooking rather than the larger Western bell peppers.

examples.japanese: ピーマン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{肉|にく}{詰|づ}め⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ピーマン⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧だった。
examples.english: I didn't like green peppers when I was a kid.

examples.japanese: ピーマン⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦パプリカ→パプリカ：18170_papurika⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{細切|ほそぎ}り→細切り：08571_hosogiri⟧にして⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I julienned green peppers and paprika and added them to the stir-fry.

notes:
USAGE:
ピーマン is one of the most commonly disliked vegetables among Japanese children, frequently appearing in surveys of children's least favorite foods. Common dishes include ピーマン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{肉|にく}{詰|づ}め (meat-stuffed peppers) and {青椒|チンジャオ}ロースー (pepper steak stir-fry).

NOTE ON SCOPE:
Larger, colorful bell peppers (red, yellow, orange) are usually called ⟦パプリカ→パプリカ：18170_papurika⟧ in Japanese, while ピーマン refers to the smaller green variety.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ピーマン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{肉|にく}{詰|づ}め (meat-stuffed green peppers)
- ピーマン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{炒|いた}める→炒める：01879_itameru⟧ (stir-fry green peppers)
- ピーマン⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{種|たね}→種：02157_tane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (remove green pepper seeds)

ETYMOLOGY:
From French "piment" (pepper).
